title: AI Brand Monitoring: What to Track & Which Tools
excerpt: AI brand monitoring checks what ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini say about your brand. Learn how it differs from social listening, what to monitor and how often.
keywords: AI brand monitoring vs social listening
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
AI brand monitoring is the ongoing practice of checking what AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini say about your brand: whether they mention you, whether the facts are right, how they frame you, which sources they cite and which competitors they recommend instead. Classic brand monitoring watches what people publish on the web and social media. AI brand monitoring watches what machines generate in answers that are never published. It needs its own method, its own metrics and a regular review rhythm.

This post explains what AI brand monitoring is, how it differs from social listening and traditional brand monitoring tools, what to monitor, and how to set up a process your team can keep running. For the hands-on, step-by-step measurement method, see our pillar guide on [how to track brand visibility in AI platforms](/blog/how-to-track-brand-visibility-in-ai-platforms).

## What is AI brand monitoring?

Brand monitoring has always meant keeping an eye on what is said about you: press coverage, reviews, social posts, forum threads. AI brand monitoring extends that to a new kind of speaker, the AI assistant.

When a buyer asks "What's the best accounting software for freelancers?" or "Is [your brand] any good?", the assistant writes an answer on the spot. That answer may recommend you, skip you, describe you accurately or repeat something out of date. Nobody publishes it, nobody tags you, and it won't show up in your analytics. Unless you check, you don't know.

AI brand monitoring answers five questions on a regular basis:

1. **Are we mentioned** when buyers ask about our category?
2. **Is what the AI says about us accurate?**
3. **How are we framed:** positively, neutrally or with caveats?
4. **Which sources** do assistants cite or rely on when they talk about us?
5. **Which competitors** are recommended, and are they gaining on us?

The term is sometimes used in a second sense: using AI (for example, machine learning for sentiment analysis) to monitor ordinary web and social mentions. That is AI-*powered* brand monitoring, and most listening tools include some of it. This article is about monitoring your brand *inside* AI answers, which is the newer and less-covered problem.

## Why AI brand monitoring matters now

AI answers are short, so being left out of a few named options costs more than ranking low on a long results page. Errors also repeat silently: if an assistant states the wrong price or a discontinued plan, everyone who asks hears it. And assistants can also browse the web (ChatGPT can [search the web and link its sources](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), and [Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352895-how-does-perplexity-work) and [Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/web-search) search too), so today's reviews and roundups can shape tomorrow's answers. Our [AI brand visibility guide](/blog/ai-brand-visibility-guide) covers the bigger picture.

## AI brand monitoring vs social listening and traditional brand monitoring

The most common misconception is that an existing monitoring setup already covers AI. It usually doesn't, because classic tools watch *published* content and AI answers are generated privately for each user.

| | Traditional brand monitoring and social listening | AI brand monitoring |
|---|---|---|
| **What it watches** | Published content: news, blogs, social posts, reviews, forums | Answers generated by AI assistants in response to prompts |
| **How data is collected** | Crawling and indexing public pages and social feeds | Sending prompts to the assistants and analyzing the replies |
| **Unit of measurement** | Mentions, reach, engagement, sentiment of posts | Mention rate across prompts, position in answers, accuracy, sentiment, citations, share of voice |
| **Typical alerts** | New mention, spike in volume | Usually periodic reviews of trends rather than instant alerts, because single answers are noisy |
| **Main use** | PR, reputation, customer care, campaign tracking | Visibility in AI recommendations, accuracy of AI descriptions, competitive position |

### What popular monitoring tools actually cover

It's worth checking vendors' own documentation, because the market is changing quickly. As of October 2026:

- **Google Alerts** emails you when [new results for a topic show up in Google Search](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/4815696). It does not report what AI assistants say.
- **Mention**'s [homepage](https://mention.com/en/) describes monitoring topics across social media and the web; it doesn't describe AI-answer monitoring there, so ask the vendor if that matters to you.
- **Brand24**, a social listening tool, now offers a separate [AI Visibility](https://brand24.com/ai-visibility/) product powered by Chatbeat. Brand24's page says it runs prompts across assistants including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, and reports visibility, share of voice, sentiment and cited sources.
- **Meltwater** offers [GenAI Lens](https://www.meltwater.com/en/products/genai-lens), which it describes as AI brand monitoring for LLM visibility, covering assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity alongside its media monitoring.
- **SEO suites** such as Semrush ([AI Visibility Toolkit](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1493-ai-visibility-toolkit)) and Ahrefs ([Brand Radar](https://ahrefs.com/brand-radar)) have added AI modules too, with different platform lists (see our [AI brand visibility tracker](/blog/ai-brand-visibility-tracker) guide).

So the accurate picture is this: the classic web and social feeds don't see AI answers, but some established vendors now sell AI monitoring as a separate module, alongside dedicated AI visibility tools. Coverage differs a lot between them, so compare which assistants each one queries, whether you can choose the prompts, and how often they run.

Classic listening still matters: the reviews, articles and threads it finds are often the sources assistants cite. Listening shows what is published; AI monitoring shows what the assistants make of it.

## What to monitor in AI answers

A useful AI brand monitoring program tracks five things. Each one answers a different business question.

### 1. Mentions and visibility

Are you named when buyers ask category questions ("best X for Y"), problem questions ("how do I fix Z?") and comparison questions ("X vs Y")? Measure this as a **mention rate**: the share of prompt runs in which your brand appears. Also note **position**, because being named first carries more weight than being the sixth name in a list.

Watch the gap between brand prompts and category prompts. If assistants describe you well when asked about you by name but rarely recommend you in category answers, they know you but don't associate you with the category.

### 2. Accuracy

This is the part classic monitoring never covered and the one most likely to cost you deals. Check what assistants say about:

- Pricing and plans
- Core features and integrations
- Who the product is for
- Company facts (name, location, ownership, founding story)
- Confusion with similarly named companies

Accuracy problems are often the fastest to fix, because they usually trace back to a specific source: an old press release, an outdated directory listing, a stale page on your own site.

### 3. Sentiment and framing

Is the mention positive, neutral or negative? More importantly, what label does the assistant attach to you: "best for enterprises", "budget option", "hard to set up"? Framing decides which buyers the assistant sends your way. A neutral mention with the wrong framing can hurt more than an occasional negative one.

### 4. Citations and sources

For assistants that show sources, such as [Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352895-how-does-perplexity-work) and [ChatGPT when it searches](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), record which URLs appear when you're mentioned and which appear when a competitor is mentioned and you're not. This is often the most actionable data you'll collect. If the same review site, directory or comparison article keeps appearing, getting listed or corrected there is a direct path into the answer.

Also make sure the assistants' search crawlers can reach your site; blocking one by accident can keep your own pages out of cited answers (see [OpenAI's crawler docs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) on OAI-SearchBot). Our [AI brand visibility guide](/blog/ai-brand-visibility-guide) lists which crawler does what.

### 5. Competitors and share of voice

Which competitors do assistants recommend for your key prompts, and how often compared with you? **Share of voice**, your mentions divided by the total mentions of you and your tracked competitors, is the best single number for this. Our guide to [AI share of voice](/blog/ai-share-of-voice) covers the formulas and worked examples.

## How to set up an AI brand monitoring process

Monitoring only works if it runs consistently and someone acts on it. The detailed measurement steps are in our [step-by-step tracking guide](/blog/how-to-track-brand-visibility-in-ai-platforms); this section covers the program around them.

### Define scope and prompts

Decide which brands, products, competitors and assistants you monitor (for most brands: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini), then write 20 to 50 buyer-style prompts and freeze the wording so trends stay comparable.

### Choose how you'll collect answers

- **Manually** in a spreadsheet: free, transparent, and the best way to learn your landscape, but slow once you sample several runs per prompt across four assistants.
- **With a tool:** a dedicated AI visibility tool or an AI add-on from your listening or SEO vendor. Compare platform coverage, prompt control, scoring transparency and how results are stored over time.

AI Brand Track is one option for collecting a baseline quickly. You enter your website URL, and it extracts your brand, industry and keywords, finds competitors and queries ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini with industry prompts. In about 60 seconds you get a 0-100 visibility score, competitor rankings, which prompts mention you, sentiment, share of voice and recommendations. You can save analyses and compare them over time, and AI Brand Track also runs automatic weekly checks with a trend graph and a weekly email. Tracking is weekly, not daily, so add an extra analysis after a launch or major content change.

### Assign ownership

AI brand monitoring touches several teams. A simple split:

- **SEO or content** owns the prompt set, the measurements and the content fixes.
- **PR and communications** own third-party coverage and corrections on external sources.
- **Product marketing** owns positioning and accuracy of product facts.
- **Sales and support** report what prospects say an AI told them, often the first sign of an accuracy problem.

### Set a cadence

| Cadence | What to do |
|---|---|
| **Monthly** | Full run of your prompt set across all assistants; compare mention rate, share of voice, sentiment and accuracy issues with last month |
| **Every one or two weeks** | Re-check your 5-10 most important category prompts if you're actively working on visibility or in a fast-moving category |
| **After key events** | Re-run after a launch, rebrand, pricing change, major PR moment or a known AI model update |
| **Quarterly** | Review the prompt set itself, the competitor list and which assistants you cover |

Because answers vary between runs, judge changes across several cycles rather than reacting to a single answer. Our post on [AI model drift detection](/blog/ai-model-drift-detection) explains how to tell real movement from noise.

### Turn findings into actions

Give every finding an owner and a fix: correct the source behind inaccurate facts, publish category and comparison pages where you're missing, and study the sources now cited for competitors who are gaining. Our tracking guide's section on acting on results, plus [how to get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT](/blog/how-to-get-your-brand-mentioned-in-chatgpt) and our overview of [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization), cover the fixes in depth.

## Choosing AI brand monitoring tools

When you compare AI brand monitoring tools, ask:

1. **Which assistants does it query?** Make sure the list matches where your buyers ask questions.
2. **Can you see the prompts and answers?** A score without the underlying answers is hard to trust or act on.
3. **Can you choose or edit prompts,** or are they generated for you?
4. **How does it handle variability?** Look for repeated runs or clear sample sizes.
5. **Does it track accuracy, sentiment and citations,** or only mentions?
6. **How do re-runs work** (scheduled or on demand), and what does your cadence cost?

## FAQ

### What is AI brand monitoring?

AI brand monitoring is the regular practice of checking what AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini say about your brand. It covers whether you're mentioned, whether the information is accurate, how you're framed, which sources are cited and which competitors are recommended. It complements traditional brand monitoring, which watches published web and social content.

### How is AI brand monitoring different from social listening?

Social listening tracks what people publish on social media, news sites, blogs and forums. AI brand monitoring tracks what AI assistants generate in answers, which are created per conversation and not published anywhere a crawler can find. That's why it works by sending prompts to the assistants and analyzing the replies, rather than by indexing public pages.

### Do tools like Google Alerts or Brand24 monitor ChatGPT?

[Google Alerts](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/4815696) does not; it reports new Google Search results. Brand24 now sells a separate [AI Visibility](https://brand24.com/ai-visibility/) product (powered by Chatbeat), and Meltwater offers [GenAI Lens](https://www.meltwater.com/en/products/genai-lens), so check each vendor's current documentation for which assistants it covers.

### How often should I monitor my brand in AI assistants?

Monthly is a sensible default for a full review, with more frequent checks on a few priority prompts if you're actively working on visibility. Also re-run after launches, pricing changes, PR events or known model updates. Keep the prompt set fixed so results are comparable over time.

### Can AI brand monitoring send real-time alerts?

Some tools offer scheduled runs or notifications, but single AI answers are noisy, so instant alerts on one changed answer can mislead. Most teams get more value from periodic reviews of trends across many prompts and runs. If a tool you're evaluating advertises alerts, ask how it separates real changes from normal variation.

## Start with a baseline

If your buyers use AI assistants to research brands, what those assistants say about you is worth checking as routinely as your reviews or press coverage. Start with a fixed prompt set, measure mentions, accuracy, sentiment, citations and competitors, and review the trend on a set schedule.
